checked.claim: fixed: the Eclipse explainer no longer says 'move once, anywhere'; {reach} follows overflowCrossings(ECLIPSE_MOVES), and the darkening pitfall is covered
checked.why: The main defect is gone (the sentence gives the connected-room reach and free placement at night). But the reader's 'the old pitfall (darkness lowers the allowance) is covered' does not hold: the old finding's pitfall was the darkening. Under the darkness Overflow, overflowCrossings(2) gives 1, so the sentence reads 'up to 1 connected room or anywhere at night' - while the same darkening pulls the Night Eclipse's free placement back to two crossings (freeBecomes: ECLIPSE_MOVES; overflowCrossings(null) answers 2). The clause 'or anywhere at night' is fixed text and is not taken back under the darkening, and eclipseExplanation is the only builder (phaseExplanation calls it with no argument while clock.eclipse). So in a darkened Night Eclipse the player's 'Where things stand' window promises free placement the movement code does not give, and understates the night's two crossings as one. A particular situation of the same class (the text overstates free placement): partly, minor. R1160 holds the number's road, not the night clause.
